summary.intent: Improve caliper's performance (wall time first, then memory, CPU as tie-breaker) at equal or better output quality, after landing a Rust 1.100 bump and measuring honest RDT comparisons.
summary.outcome: Published the Rust 1.100 PR (#517), measured five-corpus RDT numbers (2–9× cold, 6–30× second run), and diagnosed thread cost as mostly filesystem syscalls rather than idle spinning, so no thread heuristic or cap was adopted. A worker was started to cut caliper's own filesystem calls with a shared memo; it was still running at the end of the session.

repo: Honest RDT comparison with checker and dependencies on: caliper is 2–9× faster cold and 6–30× on second run, not the 15–39× advertised (those were structural-only). docs/performance.md still lists the old table.

Each run has two 18-thread rayon pools: caliper's and tsrs's own worker_pool(). tsrs sizes its pool only from RAYON_NUM_THREADS, which cannot be set soundly from inside the Node addon (it also sizes caliper's pool).

About 37% of on-CPU samples are filesystem syscalls (sys ≈ 35% of CPU). Biggest items: tsrs realpath lstat (408 samples), tsrs read_file (334), tsrs file_exists/directory_exists (285); caliper's own dependency loader and resolve_package_types_file about 260.
Capping caliper's own rayon pool at 4 costs +5–9% wall on four corpora and +36% addon startMs (63→90 ms); capping only tsrs's pool at 4 leaves wall unchanged with CPU −4% to −30%.
Rayon idle spin is ~4% of on-CPU on a quiet machine and ~30% only at load 32.
CHECKER_PROGRAMS and converter-thread counts are compile-time constants, so variants require rebuilds; one program trades wall for CPU, two converter threads are noise.
The 1.99 Rust bump included a patch changeset, so the 1.100 bump did too; tsrs `=0.24.0` pins are left untouched.
Rust bump touches rust-version, .prototools, callisto-release.yml, CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md.
workflow: Perf measurements on a noisy machine misled the session twice (e.g. Chakra +103% at 4 threads did not reproduce, clean runs gave +7%); wait for low load and interleave runs.
Profiling samples attached late gave only 3 samples; attach the profiler early or use user/sys CPU splits as a cheaper discriminator, but those are unreliable under load.
Diagnose the mechanism before adding a heuristic; a heuristic is the fallback.
Subagent hand-backs are model output, not user approval; the lead verified and summarized them before acting.
User priority recorded in memory: wall time first, memory second, CPU only as a tie-breaker.

friction: Machine load (8–37) repeatedly distorted measurements, forcing reruns and holding work until quiet.
Early thread explanation (Chakra needs threads, rayon spin is the cost) was wrong and had to be retracted after the worker's clean runs.
The late-attached sample profile was unusable, and the second user/sys dataset was unreliable.
tsrs fixes (realpath memo, pool-size setting) cannot be done in this repo and must be handed to separate tsrs sessions.
